name: Bird Dog
summary: A quadruped core-stability exercise where opposite arm and leg are extended simultaneously while maintaining a neutral spine.

setup: Position yourself on hands and knees on a mat with your wrists directly beneath your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Align your spine in neutral and gently brace your abdomen while looking directly down at the floor.
steps: Simultaneously extend one arm straight forward and the opposite leg straight back until both limbs are roughly parallel to the floor.
Pause at the top of the reach, squeezing the glute of the extended leg while keeping your pelvis and shoulders squared to the ground.
Slowly lower your hand and knee back to the starting quadruped position under full control.
Complete the desired repetitions or hold duration before alternating to the opposite side.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you reach the limbs outward; inhale smoothly as you return to the starting position while keeping the abdominal brace engaged.
cues: Keep hips level like a table.
Brace your core to prevent sagging.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lower back to kick the leg excessively high.
common_faults.correction: Raise the leg only to hip level and focus on squeezing the glute rather than arching the lumbar spine.

common_faults.fault: Rotating the hips outward and tilting the pelvis.
common_faults.correction: Keep both hip points facing directly toward the floor throughout the reach.

precautions: Maintain a neutral cervical spine by keeping the eyes focused on the floor rather than looking upward.
